item.title: An equiregular counterexample to the Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Lerario, Rizzi and Tiberio disproved the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture with a rank-two distribution on $\mathbb R^4$, of degree of nonholonomy five at the origin, whose endpoint map from that point has no regular values. Their distribution is neither equiregular nor real-analytic, and the equiregular case has remained open. We construct an equiregular rank-two distribution on an open set diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^9$, with small growth vector $(2,3,5,8,9)$, whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values. This growth vector is maximal and generic for rank-two distributions in dimension nine, so the failure of the Sard property is not tied to any degeneracy of the growth vector. Singular curves of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio-type structure built from the same coefficient lift, inside the strip where our distribution is defined, to singular curves, and the vertical displacement of a horizontal loop is an explicit strip integral. Realising an open set of vertical displacements by singular loops reduces to a graded moment problem, which we solve with pairs of bumps of opposite winding, an anisotropic rescaling, and an inverse function theorem uniform over infinitely many scales. We also state, with proofs deferred to a planned longer version, two results about our distribution: a description of its abnormal dynamics in the cotangent bundle, which explains the example from a dynamical point of view, and the non-constancy of its Tanaka symbol. The latter motivates an equiregular counterexample in dimension twelve with constant Tanaka symbol (constant nilpotentisation), announced here and to be proved in a separate paper. The longer version will also contain obstructions to real-analytic and lower-dimensional versions, and a transversal variant of the construction, which also leads to a modification of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio counterexample.
item.dc:creator: Bangjie Wang, Igor Zelenko

item.title: Inhomogeneous balanced non-K\"ahler metrics on complex projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the cohomogeneity one action of $G_{p,q}=\mathrm{U}(p+1)\times\mathrm{U}(q+1)$ on $\mathbb{C}P^{p+q+1}$, where $p\geq q\geq 1$ and $p>1$. We characterize all $G_{p,q}$-invariant Riemannian metrics compatible with the canonical complex structure and obtain parametrizations of the invariant K\"ahler and balanced metrics. As an application, we use these parametrizations to construct a family of inhomogeneous balanced non-K\"ahler metrics with positive scalar curvature on complex projective spaces of odd complex dimension.
item.dc:creator: Brian Grajales, Lino Grama

item.title: Arithmetic Constraints on Charges of Symmetric Monopoles
item.description: arXiv:2610.24139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For Euclidean BPS monopoles with gauge group $SU(N)$, maximal symmetry breaking, and sufficiently generic spectral data, we produce necessary congruence relations that their magnetic charges must satisfy when $N \geq 3$. As such, a monopole as above with given charges can have certain subgroups of $SO(3)$ ruled out as possible groups of symmetries. In particular, the axially symmetric case may only admit non-trivial magnetic charges in the non-generic setting.
item.dc:creator: Paul Cusson

item.title: Tetrahedral points and classification of Almgren-minimizing sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.24362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a two-dimensional Almgren-minimizing set in three dimensions which is sufficiently close in Hausdorff distance to a tetrahedral cone contains an interior tetrahedral point. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative regularity near tetrahedral cones and we complete the classification of entire Almgren-minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
item.dc:creator: Michele Caselli, Zachary Lihn

item.title: Split Normal Bundles and Rigidity of Holomorphic Immersions from Compact Ball Quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.24374v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic immersion from a compact complex hyperbolic space form into a higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space form. We prove that if the normal bundle decomposes as a direct sum of holomorphic line bundles, then the immersion is totally geodesic. This result has no restriction on the codimension and extends, under the splitting hypothesis, the classical rigidity theorem of Cao--Mok. The proof uses the polarized complex variation of Hodge structure induced from the target. The line-bundle decomposition produces nef zero-Higgs line quotients, and a Chern-character identity forces the Gauss-defect form to have nontrivial nullity at every point. The null-foliation and boundary argument of Cao--Mok then shows that the defect vanishes identically. In particular, this answers a question posed by Mok almost twenty years ago about decomposable normal bundles for complex surfaces immersed in four-dimensional complex hyperbolic space forms.
item.dc:creator: Rong Du

item.title: Smooth Quasi--Einstein Lifts of Locally Embeddable Three-Dimensional CR Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24455v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a $C^\infty$ analogue of the real-analytic quasi--Einstein lifting theorem of Hill, Lewandowski and Nurowski \cite[Theorem~2.5]{HLN2008}. Every smooth, locally CR-embeddable, strictly pseudoconvex three-dimensional CR manifold admits, for each real cosmological constant, a local smooth Lorentzian quasi--Einstein lift whose null congruence is geodesic, shearfree and twisting and whose Weyl tensor has Petrov type~$\mathrm{II}$ or $\mathrm{D}$. The result extends local lifting beyond the Sasakian setting of the global constructions in \cite{GSS2020} and the local results in \cite{GGS2026}. The proof establishes smooth local solvability of the reduced semilinear contact equation by combining an $L^\infty$ contraction with subelliptic regularity.
item.dc:creator: Masoud Ganji

item.title: A counterexample to the local existence of conformal normal metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.24541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every dimension $n\ge3$, we construct a smooth Riemannian metric whose entire Taylor series at a point agrees with the Euclidean metric and whose conformal class contains no smooth conformal normal metric near that point. For the metric used in the construction, parametrized by a smooth angular function, we prove that conformal normalization forces a dimension-dependent exponential decay rate for the spherical harmonic components of that function. This gives counterexamples whenever the angular coefficients decay too slowly. In particular, every nonanalytic angular function yields a counterexample. The proof combines a weighted cylinder estimate with an integral identity relating the angular spectral coefficients of the background volume defect to the nonlinear remainder. We also give a direct counterexample to the linear right inverse used in Cao's smooth existence argument and identify the failure of angular summability in that construction.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Zhang

item.title: Equivariant Moment Maps and the Ricci Cocycle in Weighted Fujiki--Donaldson Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.24543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M,\omega)$ be a closed connected symplectic manifold of dimension $2n$,. We discuss weighted Fujiki--Donaldson theory with respect to the measure $d\nu=e^h\omega^n/n! $ for an arbitrary smooth real-valued function $h$ on $M$. We prove that the group generated by the flows of Hamiltonians that Poisson-commute with $h$ always admits an equivariant moment map for its action on the full space of $\omega$-compatible almost complex structures. The moment map takes values in the continuous dual of the Lie algebra. Its density is expressed in terms of the Hermitian scalar curvature, a local weight correction, and an $L^\infty$ function $r_h^0$ constructed from the long-time average of the polar determinant phase. The function $r_h^0$ can be regarded as a Ruelle-type asymptotic density incorporating phase comparison via a connection. The key step in the proof is to represent the Ricci cocycle as the coboundary of a continuous cochain constructed from $r_h^0$. We also consider the action of the exact volume-preserving diffeomorphism group on a connected component of the space of almost complex structures inducing the given orientation on a closed connected oriented manifold of real dimension $2n$. In contrast to the weighted Hamiltonian setting, we prove that, for $n>1$, this action admits an equivariant moment map if and only if the real first Chern class vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Ryushi Goto

item.title: Total Mean Curvature Gaps for Scalar-Flat Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a complete connected scalar-flat Euclidean hypersurface of dimension $n\geq3$ is an affine hyperplane if its normalized mean curvature has sufficiently small $L^n$ norm. We also compute the total mean curvature energy of a classical rotational scalar-flat family to show that finiteness cannot replace smallness in dimensions $n\geq3$.
item.dc:creator: Jiuru Zhou

item.title: Poincar\'e-Type Hessian Quotient Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.24682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by the two-parameter continuity-path approach of Chen and Xu, we employ a modified continuity path to characterize the solvability of the Hessian quotient equation for K\"ahler metrics with Poincar\'e-type singularities along a divisor D, allowing simple normal crossings and self-intersections.
item.dc:creator: Linwei Zhang

item.title: K\"ahler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
item.description: arXiv:2610.24825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate that K\"ahler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Sz\'ekelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of K\"ahler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of K\"ahler-Ricci flow.
item.dc:creator: Randall R. Van Why

item.title: Index-one capillary minimal hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb R^n_+\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.24878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify complete, two-sided, properly embedded capillary minimal surfaces with nonempty boundary and Morse index one in \(\mathbb R^3_+\). More precisely, if the boundary is compact, these surfaces are catenoid truncations; if the boundary is noncompact, they are capillary hairpin surfaces. The classification extends to higher dimensions under extrinsic Euclidean volume growth and Wang--Zhang's dimension and angle conditions.
item.dc:creator: Chenghang Lu

item.title: Complete self-shrinkers with constant norm of the second fundamental form in \(\RR^4\)
item.description: arXiv:2610.24964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(X:M^3\to\RR^4\) be a complete self-shrinker with constant squared norm \(S\) of the second fundamental form. We prove that \(S=0\) or \(S=1\), and that \(X(M)\) is isometric to a hyperplane or a standard product \(\SSS^k(\sqrt{k})\times\RR^{3-k}\), \(1\leq k\leq3\). This proves a conjecture proposed by Cheng and Wei for three-dimensional hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Yu Fu, Dan Yang

item.title: The Sharp Generalized Bogomolov Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.24987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon and astheno-K\"ahler manifold. Using $L^p$-approximate critical Hermitian structures, we establish a sharp generalized Bogomolov inequality for holomorphic vector bundles on $X$, without any semistability assumption. We further characterize the equality case by studying the Hermitian-Yang-Mills flow. If equality holds, every Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration is by holomorphic subbundles, and its stable quotients admit projectively flat Hermitian metrics. If, in addition, the bundle is not $\omega$-semistable, then $X$ is projective.
item.dc:creator: Chuanjing Zhang, Xi Zhang

item.title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.25000v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(\tau^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Ann\'e and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.
item.dc:creator: Daguang Chen, Guotao Huang, Tingyu Liao

item.title: Saddle Codazzi tensor on spheres and hemisphere rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2610.25035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\geq 3$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary. We ask whether $M$ must be isometric to the standard hemisphere if $\sec_g\geq 1$, $\partial M $ is isometric to the standard unit sphere, and its second fundamental form is Codazzi. Our approach centers on saddle Codazzi tensors on round spheres, where the saddle condition requires the restriction to every tangent two-plane to have nonpositive determinant. By analyzing the associated support maps, we prove that every smooth saddle Codazzi tensor on $\mathbb S^m$ vanishes identically for $m\geq 3$. Together with Panina's examples on $\mathbb S^2$, this shows that, among unit spheres of dimension at least two, nontrivial smooth saddle Codazzi tensors exist precisely in dimension two. The vanishing theorem yields an affirmative answer to the hemisphere rigidity question for $n\geq 4$. In dimension three, we realize the nontrivial saddle Codazzi tensors provided by Panina's construction, after scaling, as the second fundamental forms of smooth perturbations of the standard hemisphere, preserving the round boundary metric and the sectional curvature lower bound. This produces counterexamples to rigidity in dimension three. Nevertheless, under the same curvature and boundary assumptions, we prove the sharp inradius estimate $r_{\mathrm{in}}(M)\leq \pi/2$, with equality if and only if $M$ is isometric to the standard hemisphere.
item.dc:creator: Jian Ge, Mijia Lai, Yuntian Zhu

item.title: The Streets--Tian conjecture on compact homogeneous quotients
item.description: arXiv:2610.25229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A Hermitian-symplectic metric is a Hermitian metric whose K\"ahler form is given by the $(1,1)$-part of a closed $2$-form. Streets-Tian Conjecture states that a compact complex manifold admitting a Hermitian-symplectic metric must be K\"ahlerian (i.e., admitting a K\"ahler metric). We study Hermitian-symplectic metrics on homogeneous complex manifolds with compact isotropy, and on their compact discrete quotients. If the transitive group is connected and unimodular, we show that an invariant Hermitian-symplectic form gives an invariant K\"ahler metric, with no lattice assumption. By averaging, the same conclusion holds for compact quotients, even if the initial metric has no invariant lift. The proof uses the top exterior power of a Hermitian-symplectic form to bound the volume functional on an invariant Aeppli slice. Applying this bound to midpoint metrics gives a uniform trace estimate. From this, volume maximization produces a balanced metric in the slice, which is also pluriclosed and hence K\"ahler. We also describe the resulting K\"ahler representative and give examples showing the role of the closed lift.
item.dc:creator: Kexiang Cao, Shuwen Chen

item.title: Classification of Isometric Immersions of Spherical and HCMU Footballs into $\E^{3}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25232v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study global isometric immersions of rotational metrics with two conical ends into Euclidean three-space. For a metric $g=\mathrm{d}u^2+f(u)^2\mathrm{d}\theta^2$ of positive Gauss curvature, we prove that vanishing endpoint traces of the weighted mixed shape coefficient $f^2b$ force every smooth isometric immersion to be rotational. The resulting congruence classes are parametrized by an integer angular covering degree bounded below by the two cone-angle parameters. The proof combines a scalar elliptic equation derived from the Gauss--Codazzi system, the maximum principle, and a global angular closing condition. For spherical footballs, isolated-singularity theory and a direct estimate in coordinates conformal for the second fundamental form establish the trace condition for every smooth immersion of the regular part. We also classify all rotational isometric immersions of HCMU footballs, including those whose curvature changes sign. When the minimum curvature is nonnegative, this classification exhausts the immersions satisfying the trace condition, and hence all immersions admitting a $C^2$ polar extension at both tips.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqiang Wei

item.title: Discrete geometry and de-Rham cohomology of graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.25302v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of discrete spaces which are built by gluing coordinate patches together into an atlas, much as a manifold is built from charts. Graphs are the main examples, and an atlas on a graph gives it a geometric structure analogous to that of a manifold. This structure leads to a cohomology theory, which we show to be a discrete analogue of de Rham cohomology. We define a "discrete coordinatized space" as a cubical set equipped with the Alexandrov topology, on which differential forms become sheaves. When the atlas is regular, the de Rham cohomology agrees with the sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf, just as in the smooth case. We compute it for several examples, including a torus graph and a graph resembling a sphere, and recover the cohomology of the corresponding surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Utkarsh Bajaj

item.title: Oriented Zoll families of minimal hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{HP}^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.25379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be either $\mathbb{CP}^n$ or $\mathbb{HP}^n$. We prove that the family $\overline{\mathcal{F}}=\{\Sigma_\sigma\}_{\sigma\in M}$ of minimal geodesic spheres in $M$ characterizes the Fubini-Study metric $\overline{g}$, that is, $\overline{g}$ is the only metric that makes these real hypersurfaces minimal. This result is related to the recent theory of Zoll families of minimal hypersurfaces $(M,g,\mathcal{F}=\{\Sigma_\sigma\})\in\mathcal{Z}$. It is conjectured that the only Zoll metric in $\mathbb{CP}^n$ is $\overline{g}$. We present evidence that suggests a similar rigidity of $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\overline{g},\overline{\mathcal{F}})$ in this context of minimal hypersurfaces. Namely, we show that a direct adaptation of Guillemin's Theorem for conformal deformations of Zoll metrics in $\mathbb{S}^2$ is not possible for $(\mathbb{CP}^n,\overline{g},\overline{\mathcal{F}})$, when $p=2n-1$ is a prime number.
item.dc:creator: Diego Guajardo

item.title: Endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:Gaussian layers and Schwarzschild deficits
item.description: arXiv:2610.25444v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $\Sigma$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. As $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $\Sigma$ converges to its area, by a theorem of Fogagnolo and Mazzieri. We establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $\Sigma$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal Jacobi equation $Jg=g^{-1}$. After a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a Gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. In dimension three, assuming in addition that $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\ge0$ along $\Sigma$, we identify the capacity deficit of $\Sigma$ relative to the Schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $\Sigma$ is round and $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.
item.dc:creator: Sehong Park

item.title: Closed locally symmetric spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.25542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present some results concerning the geometry and dynamics of closed locally symmetric spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Souheib Allout

item.title: Elliptic closed geodesics on non-negatively curved Finsler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.25579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a compact simply-connected manifold $(M,F)$ with a bumpy irreversible Finsler metric $F$ whose flag curvature $K$ satisfies $K\ge 0$ and $H^*(M;\Q)\cong T_{d,n+1}(x)$ for some $d\in2\N$ and $n\in\N$ carries exactly $\frac{dn(n+1)}{2}$ (the number of closed geodesics in Katok's example) closed geodesics, then there are at least $2$ irrationally elliptic closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.
item.dc:creator: Wei Wang

item.title: Infinitesimally polar Killing foliations via geometric resolutions
item.description: arXiv:2610.25582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the strong Molino conjecture for complete infinitesimally polar singular Riemannian foliations and identify their Molino sheaves with those of their geometric resolutions. The resolution preserves basic and equivariant basic cohomology and transverse curvature bounds. These comparisons yield orbifold models and approximations of leaf-closure spaces, Euler localization, closed-leaf existence and Euler positivity under positive curvature, and transverse sphere theorems. Maximal defect gives a closed-ball leaf-closure space. Further applications include fundamental-group growth bounds and closedness under nonpositive transverse Ricci curvature that is negative definite at one regular point.
item.dc:creator: Francisco C. Caramello Jr., Laura Ribeiro dos Santos

item.title: Minimal immersions by first eigenfunctions of Riemann surfaces with large conformal automorphism groups. The Klein quartic
item.description: arXiv:2610.25592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimal immersions of closed surfaces into spheres by first eigenfunctions play an important role in both the theory of minimal surfaces and spectral geometry. In this paper, we establish the existence of equivariant conformal minimal immersions of this type for Hurwitz surfaces and other families of %Riemann surfaces with large automorphism group. Finally, we explicitly construct a conformal minimal equivariant immersion of the Klein quartic into the unit sphere $S^{7}$ by first eigenfunctions. Ths immersion is a natural candidate for maximizing the normalized $\lambda_1$ among closed genus-3 surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Ros

item.title: Tensorial pinching by deforming curvature cones in higher codimension mean curvature flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.25610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.
item.dc:creator: Tsz-Kiu Aaron Chow

item.title: Combinatorial Calabi flows on infinitely triangulated surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.25745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the combinatorial Calabi flow associated with vertex scalings on infinitely triangulated surfaces with piecewise Euclidean and piecewise hyperbolic metrics. Under the assumptions of uniformly bounded vertex degree and an $\epsilon$-uniformly nondegenerate initial metric, we establish short-time existence of smooth solutions and prove uniqueness among solutions that are continuous in the $L^\infty$ norm.
item.dc:creator: Yuerong Bian, Xu Xu

item.title: Principal bundles in supersymmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.25811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss rather basic problems on super principal bundles for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds (over $\mathbb{R}$) and analytic supermanifolds over a complete field of arbitrary characteristic. Sharper answers are obtained for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds and for homogeneous supermanifolds. Among others, it is proved for $C^{\infty}$-supermanifolds that given a $C^{\infty}$-supermanifold $B$ and a super Lie group $G$, there is a natural one-to-one correspondence (up to isomorphism) between the $G$-super principal bundles over $B$ and the $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$-principal bundles over $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$, where $G_{\mathrm{rd}}$ (resp., $B_{\mathrm{rd}}$) denotes the ordinary Lie group (resp., manifold) associated with $G$ (resp., $B$). To prove this, we show a generalized, equivariant version of the renowned Batchelor Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Akira Masuoka

item.title: Quantitative stratification and optimal regularity for stationary $J$-holomorphic maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.25813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give an alternate proof of the $\epsilon$-regularity theorem of Wang [Comm. Cont. Math. 2003] for weakly $J$-holomorphic maps by adapting the conservation law approach of Rivi\`ere [Invent. Math. 2007]. Then we adapt the powerful quantitative stratification method of Naber--Valtorta [Ann. Math. 2017] to obtain optimal volume estimates and rectifiability for the quantitative strata of stationary $J$-holomorphic maps. In contrast with general harmonic maps, the almost complex equation gives rise to an additional symmetry improvement: Every odd-dimensional translation symmetry extends to an even-dimensional one. Consequently, consecutive even and odd strata coincide, and the $k$-th quantitative stratum satisfies a tubular-neighborhood estimate with exponent $2m-2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, where $2m$ is the real dimension of the domain. The corresponding strata are $2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$-rectifiable, with almost-everywhere unique complex planes of symmetry. Finally, we prove that every stationary $J$-holomorphic map is smooth if the target { manifold} admits no non-constant $J$-holomorphic sphere, improving the corresponding theorem of Wang.
item.dc:creator: Chang-Yu Guo, Ming-Lun Liu, Chang-You Wang

item.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2610.25831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.
item.dc:creator: Greg\'orio Silva Neto

item.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-expanders
item.description: arXiv:2610.25833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the self-expanders of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$. Apart from the Clifford minimal cone, every such hypersurface is complete, proper and noncompact, and belongs to one of three families: two one-parameter families of embedded hypersurfaces diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{p+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{q}$ or to $\mathbb{R}^{q+1}\times\mathbb{S}^{p}$, whose profile curves leave an axis, and a two-parameter family diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{p}\times\mathbb{S}^{q}$, parametrized by the point of the profile curve closest to the origin, which is the generic family: its set of initial conditions is open and of full measure in the phase space. Every end is asymptotically conical, with explicit decay rates, and every such hypersurface has Euclidean volume growth. A profile curve of the third family has at most one loop, and the point of the curve closest to the origin lies on that loop.
item.dc:creator: Greg\'rio Silva Neto

item.title: Constant mixed Chern curvature on complete type-A flag manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.25864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the complete flag manifold SU(m)/T m-1, with m >= 3 and its standard complex structure, admits no invariant Hermitian metric with constant mixed Chern curvature when the coefficient of the holomorphic sectional curvature is nonzero. This extends the preceding nonexistence result for a particular Wallach metric on SU(3)/T2 to all invariant Hermitian metrics and to complete type-A flags of arbitrary dimension. Curvature evaluations on holomorphic root spheres contradict a necessary trace identity, covering both Kahler and non-Kahler invariant metrics and excluding both zero and nonzero curvature constants.
item.dc:creator: Yuqin Guo, Donmei Zhan

item.title: Two-step nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by quivers and geometric structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.25883v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the study of geometric structures on nilmanifolds, two-step nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by graphs play an important role. Recently, additional examples of nilpotent Lie algebras have been constructed from finite quivers without cycles. These latter examples can have arbitrarily high degrees of nilpotency, and admit Riemannian Ricci soliton metrics. In this paper, we study nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by finite quivers without cycles that are two-step nilpotent, and we prove that they can also be obtained by graphs. Using this relationship, we demonstrate that every two-step nilpotent Lie algebra obtained by a finite quiver without cycles admits a pseudo-Riemannian Ricci-flat metric. Additionally, we also classify these nilpotent Lie algebras that admit symplectic structures.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Proceedings of The 24th International Workshop on Differential Geometry of Hermitian Symmetric Spaces & Ricci Flow, Vol.24, 129--136 (2023)
item.dc:creator: Fumika Mizoguchi

item.title: A characterization of Griffiths semipositivity by top-degree optimal $\bar \partial$-estimates
item.description: arXiv:2610.25900v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a singular Hermitian metric $h$ on a vector bundle agrees almost everywhere with a Griffiths semipositive metric if its dual metric $h^*$ is locally integrable and the $\bar \partial$-equation admits solutions with optimal $L^2$-estimates for $(n,n)$-forms, where $n$ is the dimension of the base manifold. In particular, under this integrability assumption, Nakano semipositivity in the sense of optimal estimates implies Griffiths semipositivity.
item.dc:creator: Shin-ichi Matsumura

item.title: On nilpotent Lie algebras arising from parabolic subalgebras and quivers --- three-step cases
item.description: arXiv:2610.25903v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nilpotent Lie groups are important subjects for studying spacial left-invariant geometric structures. However, nilpotent Lie groups are impossible to classify, and even the two-step case has not been classified. There are several classes of examples of nilpotent Lie algebras that arise with higher nilpotency steps. In this paper, we focus on two of these methods. The first one is the nilpotent parts of parabolic subalgebras of semisimple Lie algebras. The second one is the nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by quivers. We list and compare nilpotent Lie algebras obtained by these two methods that are three-step and of dimension at most 10.
item.dc:creator: Fumika Mizoguchi

item.title: Sphere Theorems for $\frac{10}{3}$-Positive Curvature Operator of the Second Kind
item.description: arXiv:2610.26269v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that every connected closed Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\geq4$ with $\frac{10}{3}$-positive curvature operator of the second kind is diffeomorphic to a spherical space form. We also obtain a classification of connected closed Riemannian manifolds with $\frac{10}{3}$-nonnegative curvature operator of the second kind. The key step is to show that $\frac{10}{3}$-positivity implies the PIC1 condition. Finally, we give an example showing that $\frac{10}{3}$ is optimal for deducing PIC1 from $\alpha$-positivity.
item.dc:creator: Haiqing Cheng, Kui Wang

item.title: Willmore energy and minimal fillings
item.description: arXiv:2610.26331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For each $n\geq 4$, we show that the infimal Willmore energy of a non-orientable surface of odd genus immersed in $\mathbb{S}^n$ is attained by an index $(n+1)$ minimal surface in this class. For $n=4$, we obtain in addition the analogous conclusion for surfaces with non-zero Euler number. The proof uses the fact that such surfaces represent a non-trivial cobordism class together with an observation of M. Gromov relating the conformal area in $\mathbb{S}^n$ to minimal fillings in the hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}$.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bernstein, Daniel Ketover

item.title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in space forms with harmonic curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.26376v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A biconservative hypersurface $M$ in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ is a hypersurface whose normal part of the vector $\Delta\vec{H}$ vanishes. We study such hypersurfaces with harmonic curvature or parallel Ricci curvature, and prove that have constant mean curvature. Also, by combining our results with previous results of H.B. Lawson Jr. and M. Umehara we obtain that if $M$ is a biconservative hypersurface in a space form $\overline M^{n+1}(c)$ with parallel Ricci tensor or harmonic curvature, then the shape operator $\bold{A}$ of $M$ is covariant constant, i.e. $\nabla\bold{A}=0$.
item.dc:creator: Ram Shankar Gupta, Andreas Arvanitoyeorgos, Marina Statha

item.title: From Chaplygin Sleigh to Torpedo: An~example of a~Cartan-Geometric View of Left-Invariant Nonholonomic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.26439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We discuss two models of a 3D torpedo in which the centre of mass $x$ moves only longitudinally, while the body may rotate about $x$. Although these are simple examples of left-invariant distributions on the Lie group $SE(3)$, they possess rich geometric structures. For the simplest model, we arrive at an abelian extension of a flat (3,5) path geometry, while adding tiny coupling, we obtain a non-trivial hyperbolic type codimension two CR geometry whose symmetry algebra is just $\mathfrak{se}(3)$.
item.dc:creator: Pavla Musilova, Jan Slovak

item.title: Rigidity of Euclidean Convex Fillings for Ordinary Ambrosio--Kirchheim Mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.26477v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove rigidity for compact integral current fillings with respect to ordinary Ambrosio--Kirchheim mass. Let $C\subset\R^n$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, $n\ge1$, and let $T\in\I_n(X)$, where $X=\spt T$ is compact. Suppose $\iota:\partial C\to X$ is an isometric embedding for the Euclidean chord metric and \[ \partial T=\iota_\#\cur{\partial C},\qquad \M(T)=\Leb^n(C). \] Then $\iota$ extends to a surjective isometry $I:C\to X$ satisfying $I_\#\cur C=T$. No map from the filling to the convex body is assumed.
item.dc:creator: Xianfeng Jiang

item.title: Low dimensional C-spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.26481v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give the classification of C-spaces (i.e., compact homogeneous spaces admitting an invariant complex structure), up to finite cover and equivariant diffeomorphism, of dimension 6, 8 and 10. The conditions for the existence of a balanced, pluriclosed, CYT and LCK Hermitian metric are established for dimensions 6 and 8.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Lauret, Facundo Montedoro

item.title: Curvature distributions and the Steiner formula for characteristic surfaces in the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2610.26706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a new Steiner-type formula for smooth surfaces in the sub-Riemannian Heisenberg group. The main novelty is that we admit characteristic points, whose presence produces nontrivial singularities both of the distance from the surface and of its tubular neighborhood. Such singularities are reflected in the Steiner formula: the expansion up to a given order $N\geq 4$ of the volume of the $\varepsilon$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)$ of a surface $S$ is no longer polynomial, in general, taking the form \[ \mathrm{vol}(\mathcal T_S(\varepsilon)) = \sum_{j=1}^3\alpha_j\varepsilon^j+\sum_{n=4}^N \left(\alpha_n+\beta_n\log\varepsilon\right)\varepsilon^n+o(\varepsilon^N),\qquad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0^+ . \] More precisely, under a geometric stability condition on characteristic points, we prove that the first three coefficients are integrals over $S$ of locally integrable curvature densities, coinciding with those known in the non-characteristic case. A new phenomenon appears at order $4$, equal to the homogeneous dimension of the Heisenberg group, where logarithmic terms may occur. We show that the higher-order coefficients are naturally described by a distributional analogue of Federer's curvature measures, whose logarithmic components are supported on the characteristic set. We compute the fourth-order coefficients explicitly. The proof is based on different ingredients of independent interest: (i) an explicit formula for the cut time of homogeneous surfaces, (ii) a fine analysis of the normal exponential map through blow-ups, (iii) the study of the stability of the surface cut locus under perturbations.
item.dc:creator: Davide Barilari, Eugenio Bellini, Tommaso Rossi

item.title: Elastic knots: compactness, contact, and variational structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.26823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study bending-minimizing sequences of closed curves in a fixed knot class and the self-contact of their limits. A positive matrix-valued measure records a possible loss of curvature energy. Ambient variations, localized on arbitrary coincidence sets, force this measure to vanish and give strong convergence in $H^2$. We then derive the elastic equation on isolated strands and overlap bundles, describe the distribution that remains at contact, and prove balance and rigidity statements under their precise additional hypotheses. Equality in the bridge bound gives constant curvature. Combining strong compactness with quantitative competitors gives an alternative proof that elastic limits in classes with equal bridge and braid indices are covered circles. An independent recovery theorem identifies the strong $H^2$ closure with the regular $H^2$ part of the $C^1$ closure and also implies strong compactness. Finally, a whole-line contact model illustrates which estimates are needed for finer shape selection.
item.dc:creator: Philipp Reiter, Heiko von der Mosel

item.title: Variational mean curvatures for general $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.24224v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The notion of variational mean curvature (VMC) arises from Massari's variational approach to hypersurfaces of prescribed mean curvature and expresses a minimizing property for Massari's functional. Here, we complement the theory of VMCs with a new sharp relation between hypersurface regularity and VMC integrability. In fact, our main result asserts that every bounded open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ boundary, $0<\alpha<1$, has a global VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for every $p<\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}$. In addition, we underpin sharpness of this conclusion by constructing examples of bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ boundary which do not admit a VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for any $p>\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}$. Our proofs are based on Barozzi's level-set construction of global VMCs and determine integrability of these VMCs by geometric investigation of their superlevel sets and of related unions of balls.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Schmidt, Jule Helena Sch\"utt

item.title: Length-convexity and domination for Hitchin representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.24606v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\geq 2$. For any $n\geq 3$, let $\text{Hit}_n(S)$ be the Hitchin component and let $\text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ be the subset of representations that take values in $\mathrm{PSp}_{2m}(\mathbb{R})$ if $n=2m$ and $\mathrm{PSO}(m,m+1)$ if $n=2m+1$. In this note we prove that for any Hitchin representation $\rho \in \text{Hit}_n(S)$ there is $j \in \text{Hit}_n(S)^\prime$ such that $\rho$ dominates $j$ in the Hilbert length spectrum; this confirms a conjecture of Lee-Zhang and, independently, Tholozan who had proved this for $n=3$. The key step is establishing a convexity of the Hilbert length function in the Bonahon-Dreyer parametrization of $\text{Hit}_n(S)$; this uses a result from the recent work of Barman-Gupta. We also prove these convexity and domination results for translation length functions and their spectra.
item.dc:creator: Subhojoy Gupta

item.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions II
item.description: arXiv:2610.24703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This is the second of two papers on isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation on manifolds with nonflat background metrics. In the first paper, we proved that, in dimensions $3\le n\le29$, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a radial model singular solution in the flat metric on the Euclidean space with origin as its singular point---a Fowler solution. In the present paper, we show that this dimension range is sharp. More precisely, for each $n\ge30$, we construct a smooth metric on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ and a positive solution of the corresponding Yamabe equation having an isolated singularity, near which the solution blows up along a sequence at a rate much faster than that of Fowler solutions. Moreover, the singular solution defines a complete conformal metric of constant positive scalar curvature and the metric agrees with the round metric to infinite order at the singular point.
item.dc:creator: Zheng-chao Han, Qinfeng Jiang, Hua-Yang Wang, Jingang Xiong, Lei Zhang

item.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.
item.dc:creator: Paulo N. Seminario-Huertas

item.title: On the isoperimetric profile in infinite dimensional pro-Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.25088v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a nontrivial compact connected Lie group with a bi-invariant Riemannian metric. On the compact pro-Lie group $K^{\N}$ we define a weighted variation by summing the distributional variations in its Lie group coordinates. We prove that all sublevel sets with bounded $L^1$-norm and weighted variation are compact in $L^1$ if and only if the coordinate weights tend to infinity. The proof gives a quantitative estimate for approximation by Haar averages over normal subgroups, illustrating that it is possible to apply a methodology which is typical of the geometric measure theory in a specific area of the topological group theory. The resulting perimeter is invariant under left and right translations and is preserved under pullback by quotient homomorphisms equipped with quotient metrics. Isoperimetric minimizers exist at every prescribed Haar probability. For the infinite torus, the compactness condition is equivalent to properness of a weighted length on its character group and to compactness of a Fourier multiplier's resolvent. Finally, we show that locally compact noncompact groups require an additional condition of tightness, in order to be treated as an appropriate generalization of the compact case.
item.dc:creator: Eniola Kazeem (FUTA), Francesco G. Russo (UNICAM)

item.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2610.25253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $\pi_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.
item.dc:creator: Huagui Duan, Hui Liu, Wei Wang

item.title: Semi-classical Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.25255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $\Pi_{k,\leq k\mu_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, k\mu_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_k$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq k\delta)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.
item.dc:creator: Chin-Yu Hsiao, Chin Jui Yang

item.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.25602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and K\"ahler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, \theta)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical K\"ahler form $\theta$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Amp\`ere equations on Berkovich spaces.
item.dc:creator: Omid Amini, Matthieu Piquerez, Lyuhui Wu

item.title: The Eighth-Order Evolution Model for Closed Planar Curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.25719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the $L^2(ds)$ gradient flow of $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$ for smooth closed immersed planar curves. The stationary curves are precisely the multiply covered circles. We give an explicit sufficient condition under which the elastic energy is non-increasing and for each nonzero turning number, explicit small initial scale-invariant energy yields a global smooth solution with bounded positive length and exponential convergence to a fixed multiply covered circle, after reparametrisation. We note that that the qualitative rigidity and convergence results are already contained in the generalised ideal flow theory of McCoy and Wheeler. The present paper gives quantitative measure of small initial data, corrected evolution identities, and a complete argument in the case of the curvature energy $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$.
item.dc:creator: Yanlong Zhang, Li Ma

item.title: K\"ahler-Finsler rigidity of the Kobayashi metric and the K\"ahler base of weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.25890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish a rigidity theorem: for every balanced, smooth, bounded pseudoconvex domain, its Kobayashi metric is a smooth, strongly pseudoconvex, K\"ahler-Finsler metric restricted on a neighborhood of the origin if and only if the domain is a Hermitian ellipsoid, biholomorphic to the unit ball. Thus for any balanced, smooth, bounded, strictly convex, and strongly pseudoconvex domain that is not biholomorphic to the unit ball, its Kobayashi metric is a non-K\"ahler-Finsler, weakly K\"ahler-Finsler metric. We also prove that the base manifold of every weak K\"ahler-Finsler metric is K\"ahler.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoshu Ge

item.title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.26016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.
item.dc:creator: Jianchun Chu, Yaxiong Liu

item.title: Outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision
item.description: arXiv:2610.26320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. The outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. The outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. The incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting Penrose's original argument. This construction is inspired by Penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the Aichelburg--Sexl solution.
item.dc:creator: Junbin Li

item.title: A new localization approach for Willmore flows: Asymptotic analysis for the Dirichlet problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.26602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the Willmore flow with Dirichlet boundary conditions by means of a new geometric localization approach. In contrast to previous works, we do not rely on localized energy estimates, but on uniformly controlled isothermal coordinates and localized parabolic a priori estimates. For genus-zero surfaces satisfying an explicit energy condition depending only on the prescribed boundary data, we prove global existence together with a dichotomy between smooth convergence and subconvergence to a complete noncompact Willmore surface. If the initial Willmore energy is at most $4\pi$, this dichotomy reduces to smooth convergence after reparametrization, and we show that this additional threshold is optimal. As an application, we obtain an existence criterion for the stationary Dirichlet Willmore problem.
item.dc:creator: Simon Blatt, Manuel Schlierf

item.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
item.description: arXiv:2610.26613v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=w\lambda$ for real or octonion $\lambda$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(w\lambda_1)\lambda_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $\lambda_2\lambda_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Grigorian

item.title: Tight lower bounds for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.26815v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the dimension-independent first-order query complexity of minimizing a Lipschitz geodesically convex (g-convex) function on hyperbolic space. Given a ball of radius $r$ containing a global minimizer, we prove that $\Omega(\zeta_r/\epsilon^2)$ queries are necessary to attain accuracy $\epsilon Mr$, where $M$ is the Lipschitz constant and $\zeta_r=r/\tanh r$ captures the effect of curvature. This matches the known $O(\zeta_r/\epsilon^2)$ upper bound for the Riemannian subgradient method (Zhang and Sra, 2016). This is the first query-complexity result for g-convex optimization that is tight simultaneously in curvature and target accuracy. The standard Euclidean recipe of constructing hard instances as maxima of affine functions does not transfer to hyperbolic space, so the lower bound requires a new mechanism. Our starting point is the worst-function construction of Criscitiello and Boumal (2023, Appendix A). It gives the same lower bound for a subclass of algorithms, including the subgradient method, whose queries remain in prescribed g-convex regions. We retain this geometric setup and carefully tune and augment their hard function to accommodate every deterministic first-order algorithm. The key new mechanism is an advance-or-stall scheme: when a query lies in these regions, the oracle reveals at most one new information direction (advance); when a query leaves them, we show that the oracle can answer without revealing any new hidden direction (stall). Unlike earlier curvature-dependent lower bounds, the proof uses no ball-packing argument.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Criscitiello

item.title: High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow in the Complex Projective Space
item.description: arXiv:2311.01407v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the mean curvature flow of smooth, compact submanifolds of high codimension with quadratic pinching in $\mathbb{C}P^k$. We establish a codimension estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, in a quantifiable way. Under a cylindrical type pinching, this limiting flow is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. These estimates allow us to analyse the behaviour of the flow near singularities and establish the existence of the limiting flow. With a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using Stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.
item.dc:creator: Artemis A. Vogiatzi

item.title: Metric Lines in Engel-type Groups
item.description: arXiv:2405.08186v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the framework of sub-Riemannian manifolds, a natural question is: What are the ''metric lines'' (i.e., isometric embeddings of the real line)? This article presents a conjecture classifying metric lines in Carnot groups and investigates the question for Carnot groups of arbitrary rank. It focuses on metric lines in Engel-type groups, whose sub-Riemannian structure is defined on a distribution of rank $n+1$. The approach employs a novel technique, the sequence method, initially developed to study metric lines in jet space.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Bravo-Doddoli

item.title: Sharp Quartic Pinching for the Mean Curvature Flow in the Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2408.08022v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a sharp quartic curvature pinching for the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$, $m\ge2$, which generalises Pu's work on the convergence of submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$ to a round point. Using a blow up argument, we prove a codimension and a cylindrical estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, quantitatively, and is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. With a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using Stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.
item.dc:creator: Artemis A. Vogiatzi

item.title: Two Fefferman-type constructions involving almost Grassmann structures and path geometries
item.description: arXiv:2509.04878v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a Fefferman-type construction that associates an almost Grassmannian structure of type $(2,n+1)$ to every $(n+1)$-dimensional path geometry. We prove that the construction is normal and provide two equivalent characterizing conditions for all almost Grassmannian structures which locally arise from this construction: one in terms of certain parallel tractors and the other in terms of a Weyl connection of an almost Grassmann structure. We prove that the latter condition is independent of the choice of Weyl connection. We then introduce a related Fefferman-type construction associating an almost Grassmannian structure of type $(2,n+1)$ to every almost Grassmannian structure of type $(2,n)$. We prove that this construction is non-normal and characterize all almost Grassmannian structures which locally arise in this way in Cartan geometric terms.
item.dc:creator: Zhangwen Guo

item.title: Ancient Gauss curvature flows of bounded width
item.description: arXiv:2510.05614v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we construct a pancake-like ancient compact solution with flat sides to the Gauss curvature flow, contained in a slab. Also, we construct sausage-like ancient compact solutions to the $\alpha$-Gauss curvature flow with $\alpha >\frac{1}{2}$, asymptotic to a round cylinder.
item.dc:creator: Beomjun Choi, Kyeongsu Choi, Dongjun Noh

item.title: Geodesics in the Deep Linear Network
item.description: arXiv:2510.07324v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive a general system of ordinary differential equations and associated explicit solutions in a special case for geodesics between full rank matrices in the deep linear network geometry. In the process, we find horizontal straight lines in the invariant balanced manifold that remain geodesics under Riemannian submersion.
item.dc:creator: Alan Chen

item.title: Infinite rigidity of inversive distance circle packings in the Poincar\'{e} disk
item.description: arXiv:2511.09983v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The maximum principle for hyperbolic inversive distance circle packings on polyhedral surfaces is established,which unifies and generalizes existing maximum principles for various types of circle packings in the literature.As an application of this principle, a discrete Schwarz-Ahlfors lemma is established.Furthermore, an infinite rigidity theorem for weighted Delaunay triangulations of the Poincar\'{e} disk is proved,which generalizes He's hyperbolic rigidity result \cite{He2}.
item.dc:creator: Yanwen Luo, Xu Xu, Chao Zheng

item.title: Metric Lines in the Space of Curves
item.description: arXiv:2511.21065v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates sub-Riemannian geodesics in the jet space of curves. We establish the existence of two distinct families of metric lines, that is, globally minimizing geodesics, in the $2$-jet space of plane curves. This result contributes to the broader classification of metric lines in jet spaces. Additionally, we present precise criteria that characterize when a sub-Riemannian geodesic in the $2$-jet space of plane curves is a metric line.
item.dc:creator: Daniella Catal\'a, Miriam Vollmayr-Lee, Alejandro Bravo-Doddoli

item.title: Hessian geometry and Frobenius manifolds with curvature
item.description: arXiv:2512.01691v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A Hessian manifold is a Riemannian manifold such that, locally, the metric can be written as the Hessian of a function, which is called the Hessian potential. A Curved Frobenius manifold is a Riemannian manifold furnished with a commutative product that is compatible with the metric. In addition, the product's associator has to be controlled by the curvature tensor and a certain potentiality property must hold. This paper considers the interplay of Hessian and Curved Frobenius geometry. We obtain that Curved Frobenius manifolds of constant sectional curvature are consistent with a Hessian structure, if they satisfy a non-linear closed prolongation system of finite type. Locally, they are therefore characterised by purely algebraic initial data. Consistency here means that the Frobenius potential and the Hessian potential can be identified. As an application, we show that certain second-order maximally superintegrable systems locally correspond 1-to-1 to Curved Frobenius structures that are consistent with a Hessian structure.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Vollmer

item.title: Isoperimetric estimates in the product of small and large volume manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.06421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(M^m,g)$, $(N^n,h)$ be closed Riemannian manifolds, $m,n\geq 2$, with concave isoperimetric profiles and volumes $V_M$, $V_N$ respectively. We consider a one parameter family of product manifolds of the same volume, $(X,G_{\lambda})=(M^m\times N^n,\lambda^{2n}g+ \lambda^{-2m}h)$, $\lambda>0$, and estimate a lower bound for their isoperimetric profile for large $\lambda$. In particular, we show that for $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $v_0 \in (0, V_MV_N)$, one can estimate $\lambda_{0}>0$, such that for $\lambda>\lambda_0$, $$ (2\alpha-1)^{2} f_{M,\lambda}(v_0) \leq I_{(X,G_{\lambda})}(v_0)\leq f_{M,\lambda}(v_0)$$ \noindent where $f_{M,\lambda}(v)= \lambda^{-n} V_N I_{(M,g)}(\frac{v}{V_N})$ and $ I_{(M,g)}$ is the isoperimetric profile of $(M,g)$. Moreover, if $(M,g)=(S^2,g_0)$, the $2-$sphere with the round metric, and $(N,h)=(T^2,h)$, the 2-torus with the flat metric $h$, then, in this setting, we provide an interval $(v_0,V_MV_N-v_0)$ of volumes and $\lambda^*>0$, such that, for $\lambda>\lambda^*$, regions of the type ${ D^{\lambda}_R\times T^2_{\lambda} }$, with $Vol({ D^{\lambda}_R\times T^2_{\lambda} })\in (v_0,V_MV_N-v_0)$, are actual isoperimetric regions in $ (S^2\times T^2,\lambda^{2}g_0+ \lambda^{-2}h)$; being $D^{\lambda}_R$ a disk in $(S^2,\lambda^{2}g_0)$ and $T^2_{\lambda}=(T^2, \lambda^{-2}h)$.
item.dc:creator: Juan Miguel Ruiz, Areli V\'azquez Ju\'arez

item.title: Distance Functions, Curvature and Topology
item.description: arXiv:2602.17629v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss some properties of the distance functions on Riemannian manifolds and we relate their behavior to the geometry of the manifolds. This leads to alternative proofs of some "classical" theorems connecting curvature and topology.
item.dc:creator: Carlo Mantegazza, Francesca Oronzio

item.title: Finite-Gap Solutions of the Pohlmeyer--Lund--Regge Equation and the Associated Lund-Regge Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.24129v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a finite-gap construction for the Pohlmeyer-Lund-Regge (PLR) equation and the associated Lund-Regge surfaces. From the hyperelliptic spectral data we build a Baker-Akhiezer function and an SU(2)-frame, yielding an explicit theta-quotient formula for the PLR solution. We then derive criteria for s-periodicity and t-periodicity: under the stated theta-period assumptions, s-periodicity and t-periodicity are each equivalent to a critical-point condition for the corresponding normalized differential together with a phase condition at the reconstruction point. This provides a PLR analogue of the periodicity mechanism of Calini-Ivey.
item.dc:creator: Yuhei Kogo

item.title: Generalized Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence and Weil-Petersson current
item.description: arXiv:2608.15206v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we extend Hitchin-Kobayashi correspondence along holomorphic fibre space and we show that there exists a generalized Hermitian-Einstein metric which is twisted with Weil-Petersson current.In fact we generalise Song-Tian program for vector bundles
item.dc:creator: Hassan Jolany

item.title: A problem for isolated singularities of surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.19452v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the extension of the conformal structure of a Riemann surface, obtained as a submanifold of $\mathbf R^n$, across an isolated singular point, under hypotheses that are metric rather than analytic. The main result (1989) is that an isolated singularity is $\textbf{conformally point-like}$ (conformal to a punctured disc) whenever it is $\textbf{$M$-regular}$: the pair (surface minus the point, the point) satisfies a Whitney condition, and the length of the spherical slice $S(0,r)\cap E$ decreases at most linearly in $r$, a condition described as ``metric decay''. This is proved via a modulus-of-rings (extremal-length) argument, generalizing the classical planar technique to submanifolds of $\mathbf R^n$. Two classes of examples are treated: surfaces of revolution generated by a single curve, and subanalytic surfaces, for which $M$-regularity is verified directly from Hironaka's structure theory, giving as a corollary that every isolated singularity of an orientable subanalytic surface is conformally point-like. A further original result is a $C^\infty$ counterexample showing that a strict Whitney condition alone does $\textbf{not}$ imply the linear length bound: the two hypotheses in the definition of $M$-regularity are independent.
item.dc:creator: Flavio Mosca

item.title: Isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues
item.description: arXiv:2608.30807v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $n\geq 2$. We establish isodiametric-type upper bounds for Steklov eigenvalues of bounded Lipschitz domains $\Omega$ in Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$ and hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^n$. In Euclidean space, we prove \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k, \] with optimal dependence on $k$. For domains in either $\mathbb{R}^n$ or $\mathbb{H}^n$, we establish \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^2\left(\frac{|\Omega|^{\frac{1}{n}}}{D(\Omega)}\right)^{\frac{n}{n-1}}. \] The exponent of the volume-diameter ratio is optimal in both settings, and with this exponent fixed, the quadratic dependence on $k$ is also optimal. Interpolating the preceding volume-diameter estimate with a volume-normalized Steklov bound, we further obtain \[ D(\Omega)\sigma_k(\Omega)\leq C(n)k^{1+\frac{1}{2n-1}} \] in hyperbolic space. These results answer Open Question 4.37 affirmatively and resolve the hyperbolic part of Open Question 4.35, both posed in [5].
item.dc:creator: Pingxin Gu, Yao Wan

item.title: Yau's conjecture for the stacked Clifford tori of Wiygul
item.description: arXiv:2609.07423v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Yau's conjecture $\lambda_{1}=2$ for the stacked Clifford tori of Wiygul: for all integers $N\ge2$, $k,\ell\ge1$ and every sufficiently large $m$, every closed embedded minimal surface arising from Wiygul's construction, of genus $k\ell m^{2}(N-1)+1$ in the round three-sphere and resembling $N$ parallel copies of the Clifford torus joined by small catenoidal tunnels, has first Laplace eigenvalue $2$. For $N\ge3$ these surfaces are chains rather than doublings, and the even--odd decomposition on which all previous verifications for gluing constructions rest is not available. The reflection lemma of Choe and Soret reduces the problem to the sector of functions invariant under the symmetry group of the construction, and we show that the lowest nonzero eigenvalue of that sector equals $4+O(m^{-1})$. The value $4$ is the outcome of an exact identity in the limiting weighted graph model: the limiting waist ratios of the construction form the Perron vector of the adjacency operator of the line graph of a path, so that the spectral gap of the path cancels against the total conductance of the tunnels prescribed by the balancing conditions, and what survives is the coefficient of the Jacobi operator of the Clifford torus. The analytic input consists of a conformally invariant channel inequality on a cylinder and of a Poincar\'e inequality on a periodically perforated torus. The properties of the construction on which the argument rests are isolated in a reduction theorem for closed surfaces decomposed into blocks joined by families of thin channels along the edges of a finite graph, subject to a symmetry assumption and to Poincar\'e and trace inequalities on the blocks.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Pigazzini

item.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2609.25762v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be a compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold admitting a strictly positive real $(1,1)$-current $T$ with smooth $dT$ and $dd^cT\le0$. We prove that the canonical bundle $K_X$ of $X$ is nef. If every positive Lelong level set of $T$ has complex dimension at most two, then $K_X$ is ample and $X$ admits a smooth plurinegative Hermitian metric. Strictly negative Chern holomorphic sectional curvature implies Brody hyperbolicity and, when constant, forces the given metric to be K\"ahler under the latter current hypotheses. We also establish K\"ahlerness for nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature in Fujiki's class, and for nonzero constant curvature on compact complex threefolds and compact balanced fourfolds. In every complex dimension at least seven, we construct compact balanced metrics with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature, nonzero Chern curvature, vanishing of all four Chern--Ricci contractions, and a nowhere-vanishing Chern-parallel holomorphic volume form. Finally, for compact Hermitian manifolds with zero Chern holomorphic sectional curvature and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor, a smooth semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form, positive definite at one point, forces the metric to be K\"ahler flat.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin, Yuanhong Tian

item.title: Positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cones on compact complex surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2609.27870v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine the positive scalar curvature K\"ahler cone of every minimal compact K\"ahler surface of Kodaira dimension $-\infty$. By the Enriques--Kodaira classification, every such surface is either $\mathbb P^2$ or a geometrically ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $E$ is a rank-two holomorphic vector bundle over a compact Riemann surface of genus $g$. On $\mathbb P^2$, every K\"ahler class admits a K\"ahler metric of positive scalar curvature, whereas on $\mathbb P(E)$, every K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admits a metric of positive scalar curvature if and only if $g\le1$ or $E$ is slope-semistable. We further prove that if a smooth compact K\"ahler surface admits a birational morphism onto a ruled surface $\mathbb P(E)\to\Sigma_g$, where $g\ge2$ and $E$ is slope-unstable, then it contains a K\"ahler class of positive total scalar curvature admitting no positive scalar curvature K\"ahler metric. Finally, for every smooth compact K\"ahler surface $X$ birational to $Y=\mathbb P^2$ or $Y=\mathbb P(E)$, we show that K\"ahler classes admitting positive scalar curvature metrics on $Y$ are exactly the pushforwards of classes admitting such metrics on $X$.
item.dc:creator: Zehao Sha

item.title: Positive sectional curvature and non-isometric circle actions on a family of eleven-spheres
item.description: arXiv:2609.32680v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the construction of positively curved Riemannian metrics by non-isometric circle actions. For a family of homotopy eleven-spheres whose Eells--Kuiper invariants form the even subgroup of $\mathbb{Z}/992$, we construct, on each member, a smooth background metric $q$ and three effective circle actions with generators $W_1,W_2,W_3$ such that the metric determined by $g^{-1}=q^{-1}+\sum_{a=1}^3W_a\otimes W_a$ has positive sectional curvature. Each action is non-isometric for every partial metric, including its incoming metric and the final metric. We first describe the sphere by gauge transformations of the quaternionic Hopf bundle. We then construct compatible metrics on two disks and smooth their inverse metrics while preserving the action formula. A local conjugation makes the circle actions non-isometric. For each fixed member, we obtain an explicit positive lower bound $2^{-54}(1+M_{0,k}+M_{1,k})^{-28}$, where $M_{0,k}$ and $M_{1,k}$ are norms of the curvature and its first covariant derivative for its fixed connection. The bound may depend on the member of the family.
item.dc:creator: Shaoqiang Deng, Zhiguang Hu, Hui Zhang

item.title: Parabolic Monge-Amp\`ere equations on a family of Calabi-Yau manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.01202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a uniform $L^\infty$-estimate for the parabolic Monge--Amp\`ere equation under uniform H\"ormander-Tian type estimates with respect to the initial and prescribed measures. We apply this estimate to rescaled K\"ahler--Ricci flows on a family of polarized Calabi--Yau manifolds over the punctured disk. An interpolation argument gives uniform H\"ormander-Tian type estimates along the flows. We also establish uniform diameter bounds and Gromov--Hausdorff precompactness for this family of flows. In particular, we obtain an alternative proof of the diameter estimate by Li-Tosatti.
item.dc:creator: Jiyuan Han

item.title: An improved result on Chern conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.05276v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X: M^n\to \mathbb S^{n+1}(1)$ be a closed minimal hypersurface with constant scalar curvature. Chern conjecture says that a closed minimal hypersurface with constant scalar curvature, $S\geq 2n$ if $S>n$, where $S$ is the squared norm of the second fundamental form. As a partial result, Peng-Terng \cite{pt1, pt2}, Yang-Cheng \cite{yc1, yc2, yc3} and Suh-Yang \cite{sy} obtained that if $S>n$, then $S>n+ \dfrac{3}7n$. Recently, Chen \cite{c} has proved $S>n+\frac{26}{59}n$ if $S>n$. Since resolving Chern conjecture is a hard problem, as a midway for resolving Chern conjecture, one wants to prove $S>n+\frac12 n$ if $S>n$. In this paper, we give a positive solution for this midway problem. We should remark that our topological condition is complete which is weaker than closed in Chen \cite{c}.
item.dc:creator: Qing-Ming Cheng, Fengjiang Li, Guoxin Wei, Jiabin Yin

item.title: Remarks on the critical catenoid and an overdetermined eigenvalue problem in $\Bbb S^2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.06386v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It was recently proved that an embedded minimal annulus with free boundary in the unit ball $\Bbb B^3$ of the Euclidean space is, up to a rotation, the critical catenoid.
