We prove that an immersed, possibly branched, free boundary minimal annulus in $\Bbb B^3$ with embedded boundary components is necessarily free of branch points and is embedded. This shows the uniqueness of the critical catenoid holds under these weaker hypotheses. We then apply these results to prove that if $\Omega$ is a sufficiently regular annulus in $\Bbb S^2$ for which there exists a smooth function satisfying the overdetermined eigenvalue problem \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} \Delta u+ 2u = 0 \quad \text{on} \quad \Omega\\ \qquad \quad u=0 \quad \text{in}\quad\partial\Omega\\ \quad\,\,\,\, |\nabla u|=1 \quad \text{in}\quad \partial\Omega. \end{cases} \end{equation*} then $\Omega$ is, up to rotation, a rotational annulus with equatorial symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Rabah Souam (IMJ-PRG)

item.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
item.description: arXiv:2610.13405v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(\pi_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the
item.dc:creator: Catalin Carstea, Matti Lassas, Tony Liimatainen, Leo Tzou

item.title: Pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for complete Ricci flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.18364v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a uniform pseudolocality theorem for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metrics have Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius. No a priori curvature bound is assumed on the flow. As a consequence, we obtain strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows from a complete metric with the above geometric bounds. We also prove that every smooth complete Ricci flow from a complete Ricci-flat metric with uniformly positive injectivity radius is stationary. The same conclusion holds for any complete flat initial metric. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to Chen's question on the strong uniqueness of Ricci flow from Euclidean space in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: Shaochuang Huang, Zhuo Peng

item.title: Calabi metric on the space of k-Hessian potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.19653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $1\leq k\leq n$. We consider the space of smooth $k$-admissible potentials introduced in the study of the Hessian-cscK equation by Guo--Smith--Tong. The complex $k$-Hessian equation identifies this space, modulo constants, with the space of smooth positive densities of fixed total mass. We compute the differential of the Hessian density map and use it to pull back the Fisher--Rao metric. We then show that the square-root Hessian density map \[ \varphi\longmapsto 2\sqrt{\frac{\omega_{\varphi}^{k}\wedge\omega^{n-k}}{\omega^n}} \] is a global Riemannian isometry onto the positive part of the $L^2(X,\omega^n)$-sphere of radius $2\sqrt{V}$, where $V=\int_X\omega^n$. For $k=n$, this recovers the spherical description of the classical Calabi metric. We also derive the curvature, geodesic and diameter formulas, and prove a quantitative local comparison between adjacent Hessian--Fisher distances.
item.dc:creator: Linwei Zhang

item.title: Invariant complex structures on the Euclidean motion group as deformations of Calabi-Eckmann structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.20232v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_\phi.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_\phi$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$
item.dc:creator: Neda Bokan, Srdjan Vukmirovic

item.title: Classification of cubics up to affine transformations
item.description: arXiv:math/0507383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Classification of cubics (that is, third order planar curves in the $R^2$ up to certain transformations is interested since Newton, and treated by several authors. We classify cubics up to affine transformations, in seven class, and give a complete set of representatives of the these classes. This result is complete and briefer than the similar results.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Differential Geometry - Dynamical Systems, Vol.8, 2006, pp. 184-195
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Nadjafikhah

item.title: Generalizing Riemann curvature to Regge metrics
item.description: arXiv:2311.01603v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we propose a generalization of the Riemann curvature tensor on manifolds (of dimension two or higher) endowed with a Regge metric. Specifically, while all components of the metric tensor are assumed to be smooth within elements of a triangulation of the manifold, they need not be smooth across element interfaces, where only continuity of the tangential components is assumed. While linear derivatives of the metric can be generalized to Schwartz distributions, similarly generalizing the classical Riemann curvature tensor, a nonlinear second-order derivative of the metric, requires more care. We propose a generalization that combines the classical angle defect and jumps in the second fundamental form across element interfaces and argue its correctness. Specifically, if a piecewise smooth metric approximates a globally smooth metric, then our generalized Riemann curvature tensor approximates the classical Riemann curvature tensor associated with the latter. Moreover, we show that if the metric approximation converges at some rate in a mesh-dependent norm equivalent to the $L^2$ norm, then the curvature approximation converges in the negative Sobolev space $H^{-2}$, the dual space of $H^2_0$, at the same rate, under additional assumptions. By appropriate contractions of the generalized Riemann curvature tensor, this work also provides generalizations of scalar curvature, the Ricci curvature tensor, and the Einstein tensor in any dimension.
item.dc:creator: Jay Gopalakrishnan, Michael Neunteufel, Joachim Sch\"oberl, Max Wardetzky

item.title: A Table Theorem for Surfaces with Odd Euler Characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2412.01977v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use the square peg problem for smooth curves to prove a generalized table Theorem for real valued functions on Riemannian surfaces with odd Euler characteristic. We then use this result to prove the table conjecture for even functions on the two sphere.
item.dc:creator: Ali Naseri Sadr

item.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2412.17157v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map. For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent. We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup. We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e M. Mour\~ao, Jo\~ao P. Nunes, Augusto Pereira, Dan Wang

item.title: Periodic Inscription of Isosceles Trapezoids
item.description: arXiv:2503.04077v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that a pair of continuous disjoint periodic curves in $\mathbb{C}$ inscribes an isosceles trapezoid with any similarity type. The case of smooth curves can be identified with a Lagrangian intersection problem for a pair of Lagrangian cylinders in $\mathbb{R}\times S^1\times\mathbb{C}$, and the continuous case follows from the smooth one by a standard convergence argument.
item.dc:creator: Ali Naseri Sadr

item.title: The truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator
item.description: arXiv:2506.23599v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the truncated symbol of a differential symmetry breaking operator between parabolically induced representations. This generalizes the symbol map, which is defined for the case of abelian nilpotent radicals, to the non-abelian setting. The inverse of the truncated symbol map enables one to develop a recipe for the F-method for any nilpotent radical. As an application, we classify and construct differential intertwining operators on the full flag variety $SL(3,\mathbb{R})/B$ and homomorphisms between Verma modules. It turned out that, surprisingly, Cayley continuants appeared in the coefficients of one of the five families of operators that we constructed. At the end of the paper, factorization identities for the differential operators and homomorphisms are also classified. Binary Krawtchouk polynomials play a key role in the proof.
item.dc:creator: Toshihisa Kubo, V\'ictor P\'erez-Vald\'es

item.title: Levi Flat Structures via Structure Sheaves: Differential Complexes, Convexity, and Global Solvability
item.description: arXiv:2507.18341v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates Levi flat structures from the perspective of structure sheaves. We employ formal integrability to construct a class of differential complexes, thereby providing a resolution of the structure sheaf and a global realization of the Treves complex. Drawing inspiration from Morse theory and Grauert's convexity, we introduce notions of convexity and positivity that fully exploit Levi flatness, which yield global exactness of the differential complex and Sobolev regularity in the compact case. As applications, we establish the global solvability of the Treves complex for Levi flat structures, together with results on singular cohomology and the extension problem for canonical forms in the elliptic case.
item.dc:creator: Qingchun Ji, Jun Yao

item.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2509.17001v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.
item.dc:creator: Irfan Ullah

item.title: Zonal states and improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2603.12177v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish polynomially improved $L^\infty$ bounds for eigenfunctions of magnetic Laplacians on hyperbolic surfaces in the critical energy regime. We also show that, below the critical energy, the H\"ormander bound is saturated by explicit eigenstates, which we call magnetic zonal states. These states resemble zonal harmonics on the sphere and equidistribute on Lagrangian tori in phase space.
item.dc:creator: Ambre Chabert, Thibault Lefeuvre

item.title: Synthetic Differential Geometry in Lean
item.description: arXiv:2603.17457v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article is about the formalization of synthetic differential geometry with the Lean proof assistant and the mathematical library mathlib. The main result we prove and formalize is a Taylor theorem for functions of several variables, where the series expansion is around an infinitesimal neighborhood. Most of our proofs are in fact new. Our investigations highlight the possibility of using mathlib to do constructive mathematics.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Brasca (IMJ-PRG), Gabriella Clemente (IRIF)

item.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.14282v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.15981v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Dohmen, Sebastian Scholtes

item.title: Computing Fr\'echet Means on Unknown Submanifolds of Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22592v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Empirical averages are fundamental statistical primitives. On nonlinear spaces, their generalization, the Fr\'echet mean, generally lacks a closed-form solution, and its computation requires solving an optimization problem. We study the computation of intrinsic Fr\'echet means for data supported on an unknown compact $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $M_{1}$ embedded in an ambient metric space $(X,d_{\operatorname{obs}})$. Such settings arise when observations are better represented in non-Euclidean spaces, like probability distributions in Wasserstein space. We assume access only to a local sampler on $M_{1}$ and the observation metric $d_{\operatorname{obs}}$, without knowledge of its intrinsic geometry. We propose a graph-based iterative algorithm that adaptively samples the manifold and approximates geodesic interpolation. Under mild assumptions, we establish an $O(1/T)$ expected objective gap guarantee using at most $\widetilde{O}(T^{4d+3})$ sampled points. As a byproduct of our analysis we extend the metric equivalence guarantees of ISOMAP from Euclidean to Riemannian ambient spaces, which may be of independent interest. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method for computing intrinsic averages on unknown data manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Ian McPherson, Mauro Maggioni
